summary: Jane asked to book a check-up for "Friday the 17th" at 9 AM. The agent correctly said the 17th is a Saturday and offered Friday Oct 16 instead. It then blocked the booking because of an existing office visit it described as Fri Oct 23 at 9 AM with Dr. Lukowski. Ground truth has no such appointment. What is on file is Fri Oct 16 at 9:30 AM with Dr. Lukowski, plus the Mon Oct 19 follow-up. The agent then offered Oct 16 at 9:30 AM as an "opening", which is the slot Jane already holds. When the caller asked for Palo Alto, the agent said it would check Palo Alto, then repeated only Nashville times without saying whether a Palo Alto location exists. After the caller asked for "the thirty-first of November", the agent stayed silent for about 18 s and ended the call. Nothing was booked and the invalid-date probe was never answered.

expected_checks.expectation: Notices that the 17th is a Saturday, not a Friday, and resolves the conflict with the caller
expected_checks.evidence: [01:54.7] "This Friday is October sixteenth. October seventeenth falls on a Saturday. You like to book your checkup for Friday, October sixteenth at nine AM or another day?"

expected_checks.expectation: Rejects November 31st as an invalid date
expected_checks.evidence: The caller asked for "the thirty-first of November" at [04:41.6]. The agent never responded and the call ended via end_call at [05:09.0].

expected_checks.expectation: Reads back an unambiguous date and weekday for anything it books
expected_checks.evidence: Nothing was booked. Every proposed slot was stated with weekday and date (e.g. "Friday, October sixteenth at nine AM"), which is good, but no booking readback occurred.

findings.title: Reports a non-existent Fri Oct 23 9 AM appointment and misses the real Fri Oct 16 9:30 AM booking
findings.quote: You already have an office visit scheduled for Friday, October twenty third at nine AM with doctor Zebignew
findings.what_happened: Per ground truth (calls 040/044), Jane's Lukowski visit is Fri Oct 16 at 9:30 AM. The agent instead described it as Fri Oct 23 at 9 AM, repeated that several times, and used it to block the new booking. At [03:34.6] it then offered Fri Oct 16 at 9:30 AM as an open slot, which is the slot Jane already holds.
findings.why_it_matters: The caller gets a wrong picture of her schedule. She was nearly walked into rescheduling a phantom appointment, and could have been double-booked or had her real appointment overwritten.
findings.expected_behavior: Accurately report the appointments on file (Fri Oct 16 9:30 AM with Dr. Lukowski and Mon Oct 19 10 AM with Dr. Hauser). Recognise that the requested Oct 16 9 AM visit is adjacent to her existing Oct 16 booking.
findings.listen_for: Whether the agent actually says "twenty third" / "nine AM" (it is repeated consistently across 5 turns, so STT error is unlikely), and whether "nine thirty" on Oct 16 is offered as an opening.

findings.title: Agent goes silent and ends the call instead of answering the caller's date request
findings.what_happened: The caller asked whether anything was open in Palo Alto on "the thirty-first of November". The agent gave no response for about 18 s (the longest silence in the call), then ended the call without telling the caller the date does not exist or offering alternatives.
findings.why_it_matters: The caller is left with no booking and no explanation. An invalid date was neither rejected nor clarified, so the caller may still believe Nov 31 is valid.
findings.expected_behavior: Tell the caller November has only 30 days, offer Nov 30 or Dec 1 or other dates, and keep helping rather than hanging up.
findings.listen_for: The roughly 18 s of dead air after the caller's Nov 31 request, and whether the agent says anything before disconnecting.

findings.title: Says it will check Palo Alto, then repeats Nashville slots without addressing Palo Alto
findings.quote: The next opening I see is Friday. October sixteenth at nine thirty AM in Nashville.
findings.what_happened: At [04:02.6] the agent offered to check Palo Alto openings. When the caller agreed, it returned only the same Nashville times. It never said whether a Palo Alto location exists or has availability.
findings.why_it_matters: The caller cannot tell whether Palo Alto was actually searched or whether the practice simply has no Palo Alto site. This led to frustration and an unresolved call.
findings.expected_behavior: State clearly which locations the practice has. If there is no Palo Alto location, say so rather than implying a search will be done.
findings.listen_for: Any mention of a Palo Alto search result or an explanation of the practice's locations.

did_well: Caught that October 17th falls on a Saturday, not a Friday, and offered Friday October 16th as the resolution.
Verified identity by asking for the date of birth before discussing appointments.
Checked existing appointments before booking and asked whether to keep, reschedule or cancel instead of silently double-booking.
Gave each appointment with weekday, date, time and provider when listing them, and kept the Monday follow-up untouched as requested.
